title: An Electrochemical Study of the Effects of Impurities on Oxygen Evolution Electrode for Seawater Electrolysis
content: The biggest challenge for full commercial application of seawater electrolysis lies in degradation of performance, stability and durability of electrodes caused by impurity ions in natural seawater. In this study, the effects of Mg2+, Ca2+ and Cl⁻ impurity ions on activity, corrosion resistance and durability of pure nickel mesh for oxygen evolution electrode in solutions with 0.56−30.00 wt.% KOH are investigated by liner sweep voltammetry, cyclic voltammetry, Tafel plot, galvanostatic tests. The results indicate that Mg2+ and Ca2+ can induce severe degradation of activity, especially in solutions with 0.56−5.34 wt.% KOH. In addition, the corrosion current density will be reduced by Mg2+, while be increased by Cl⁻ in solutions with 0.56−5.34 wt.% KOH. Furthermore, the Mg2+ has a larger impact on durability of the pure nickel mesh in 30.00 wt.% KOH solution, while the effect of Ca2+ on durability become more significant in 0.56−5.34 wt.% KOH solutions. The Cl⁻ has smaller effects on activity, corrosion resistance and durability in all alkaline solutions. The deterioration of activity by Mg2+ and Ca2+ is mainly caused by reduction of active sites, ohmic and mass-transport resistances, while decreased corrosion current density is attributed to depletion of OH- and generation of insoluble hydroxide precipitates.
